Engravings
ĕn-grāv´ĭngz
n. pl. (cut work in stone or gold; Hebrew pittuach)
From engrave, Old English grafan, to dig or carve. The KJV uses the plural in one recurring simile: like the engravings of a signet.

Biblical Definition

Whenever Scripture speaks of engravings it is describing the work on the high priest's vestments, and it uses one comparison every time. “With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, shalt thou engrave the two stones with the names of the children of Israel: thou shalt make them to be set in ouches of gold” (Exo 28:11). The same for the golden plate on the mitre: “And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD” (Exo 28:36), and the record of its making repeats it word for word (Exo 39:30). The onyx stones were done accordingly: “And they wrought onyx stones inclosed in ouches of gold, graven, as signets are graven, with the names of the children of Israel” (Exo 39:6). A signet is not decoration. It is the mark by which a man's word is made binding and by which a document is proved his. Israel's names and the LORD's holiness were cut into stone and gold at signet depth — not painted, not stitched, but incised, so that what was written could not be lifted off.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines engraving as the act or art of cutting figures or characters on stone, metal or wood; the work so cut.

expand to see more

ENGRAVING, n. The act or art of cutting stones, metals and other hard substances, and representing thereon figures, letters or devices.

2. That which is engraved; engraved work.

ENGRAVE, v.t. To cut, as metals, stones or other hard substances, with a chisel or graver.

2. To picture or represent by incisions.

3. To imprint; to impress deeply; to infix.

Key Scripture

Exo 28:11 — "With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, shalt thou engrave the two stones with the names of the children of Israel: thou shalt make them to be set in ouches of gold."

Exo 28:36 — "And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD."

Exo 39:30 — "And they made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and wrote upon it a writing, like to the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD."

Exo 39:6 — "And they wrought onyx stones inclosed in ouches of gold, graven, as signets are graven, with the names of the children of Israel."

Modern Corruption

Identity is treated as self-declared and revisable, while Scripture cuts the names of God's people into stone at signet depth.

expand to see more

The comparison is deliberate and it is legal. A signet was pressed into wax to authenticate a document; its cut could not be argued with, and a forged seal was a capital matter. When the LORD orders the names of the tribes engraved like the engravings of a signet, He is not commissioning ornament. He is saying that the belonging of these people to Him has the standing of a sealed instrument.

This is the answer to every account of identity as a thing the self declares and may revise. The names on the onyx were not chosen by the men who bore them and could not be scratched out by them. Paul carries the figure forward when he writes that the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. What is engraved is engraved by another hand, and it holds.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew pittuach (H6603), engraving, carved work; from pathach (H6605), to open or cut in; chotham (H2368), a signet or seal, is the standard of comparison.

expand to see more

Hebrew pittuach (H6603) — engraving; Exodus 28:11, 28:36, 39:30.

Hebrew pathach (H6605) — to engrave, to cut in; the verb behind the noun.

Hebrew chotham (H2368) — signet, seal; the recurring point of comparison.

Hebrew charash (H2796) — craftsman, engraver in stone; Exodus 28:11.

Hebrew qodesh la-YHWH — HOLINESS TO THE LORD; the words cut into the golden plate.

Usage

"“Like the engravings of a signet” — the same phrase three times, never varied."

"“Grave upon it… HOLINESS TO THE LORD” — cut, not written."

"Names at signet depth: belonging with the standing of a sealed instrument."
